headline: Ward 34's rankings measure a business core's daytime crowd more than its residents.
summary:
The Loop sits inside this ward, so the denominator under most of Ward 34's rates is a resident count far smaller than the weekday crowd on its streets. Six of its strongest marks trace back to that gap. Bank branches run 23.95 per 10,000 residents here, the most of any ward, and coffee shops, gyms, licensed coffee and tea shops, and religious congregations all rank first by the same per-resident math. The 'L' logged more than 7.4 million entries at stations inside the ward last year, the highest of the 36 wards this measure covers, a count that tracks commuters and downtown crowds far more than the people who actually sleep here. That same thin denominator shows up on the worst side of the ledger too. Tobacco retailers run 16.61 per 10,000 residents here, more than in any other ward, and Ward 34 also carries the heaviest traffic exposure of any ward, an index score of 3,403.7. Both numbers measure activity that a small resident count cannot explain by itself.

A second, separate signal runs through the numbers, and it is about money rather than headcount. Ward 34 finishes last in the city on the estimated share of rent that ends up as landlord profit, above 69.8 percent under both the assessed-value and sale-price versions of that estimate. It also posts the highest share of food stores belonging to one of the 100 largest retail chains in the country, 24.36 percent, the most chain-heavy food retail of any ward in Chicago. Between the crowd-driven firsts above and this ownership pair, none of Ward 34's worst marks land on city services such as 311 response times, pothole repairs, or library and park counts.
reading_the_rankings: Two of Ward 34's numbers look contradictory before you check what each one actually measures. The ward ranks first in the city for religious congregations with paid staff, 7.09 per 10,000 residents, yet finishes last on a modeled estimate that puts 38.48 percent of adults here as having no religious affiliation. The congregation count comes from a business-registry source that spreads county-level counts across ZIP codes rather than the ward's actual boundary, so it counts staffed offices more than it counts where worshippers actually live, the same daytime-crowd pattern behind the ward's other firsts. The no-affiliation figure is a demographic model built from citywide survey patterns rather than a count of anyone's belief, and the source rates it low confidence on its own. Ward 34's last-place finish on landlord profit share deserves the same second look. Ten other wards fall inside two points of the same estimate on both the assessed-value and sale-price versions, so the ward sits at the extreme edge of a citywide cluster rather than standing alone at the bottom.

news.headline: Ald. Bill Conway Launches Reelection Bid, Ending Speculation About Mayoral Run
news.note: Conway announced he is running for reelection to the 34th Ward rather than entering the mayor's race.

news.headline: Team Behind Hyde Park's Virtue Opening Restaurant In West Loop
news.note: Chef Damarr Brown, of the Hyde Park restaurant Virtue, is opening his first solo restaurant at 219 N. Elizabeth St.

news.note: The Southern-inspired brunch spot on West Washington Boulevard announced it is closing after 36 years.
